summary: Advice on configuring dual-refill windows for sync API and long-lived background workers to avoid late-window 429s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (DataSense Labs) observed recurring soft-429s during a 5–10 minute window that coincides with a nightly background sweep job and our token refill boundary. They are running a mix of low-latency synchronous generation (short-chat requests) and a fleet of long-lived background workers that poll/generate periodically for embeddings and telemetry.

Impact:
Intermittent 429 responses for short-lived interactive traffic at ~00:00 local time for the tenant. Customer reports user-facing failures for ~3–8% of requests during the window; page reload/backoff mitigates but impacts latency and UX.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) in prod-us-west (us-west-2)
- Single tenant with route separation configured but shared burst/baseline refill windows
- Background sweep job (internal orchestrator) runs every night at 00:00 local and fanouts ~150 workers performing periodic embeddings and health checks
- Rate-limiter configured with a burst pool and sustained window; background jobs use the same API key scope as interactive routes

Steps to reproduce:
1) Schedule background sweep to run at top-of-hour (00:00) with 150 parallel workers doing short API calls (200–500ms each).
2) Send steady low-latency interactive traffic at ~10 req/s from 50 concurrent clients.
3) Observe response headers and 429s returned for interactive requests during the refill boundary.

Observed behavior:
- X-RateLimit-Remaining drops to 0 for tenant-level keys during the window.
- 429 responses show headers: X-RateLimit-Limit: 60000, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 61s (approx).
- Token refill logs show a refill epoch at 00:00 with heavy background-worker accounting inflating immediate consumption.

Expected behavior:
- Background sweep should not spike tenant-visible consumption in a way that causes interactive requests to receive 429s; or the platform should allow isolation of background vs realtime lanes (burst pool separation) so interactive traffic remains unaffected.

Attachments:
- Customer provided request timeline and sample headers (attached in ticket).
- Server-side refill trace snippets and rate-limiter logs pulled by Support (see investigation_notes).

Additional context:
Customer requests prescriptive guidance and short-term workarounds (no infra changes on their side ideally), plus recommendations for long-term config patterns for dedicated pools mixing background sweep jobs and interactive traffic.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Maya Chen (Customer): We're seeing about 3-8% 429s each night right when our nightly sweep starts at 00:00. The sweep uses the same API key credentials as our web front-end. Can Redwood recommend a config to avoid impacting users? We've attached sample headers and a request timeline.

2026-03-01 - Support (Diego Alvarez): Thanks for the report — we need three things to triage: 1) sample request IDs/time ranges for the 429s, 2) the schedule for your background sweep (timezone + concurrency), and 3) confirmation whether the background workers use short-lived ephemeral keys or the same long-lived API key. We'll pull refill and rate-limiter traces for the tenant once we have those.

2026-03-02 - Maya Chen (Customer): Provided request IDs and confirmed the sweep runs at 00:00 PDT, 150 workers, and uses the same long-lived key. Request IDs: r-20260301-01..r-20260301-93.
Also: background workers perform a keepalive ping every 30s during the sweep window for orchestration reasons.

2026-03-02 - Support (Diego Alvarez): Shared initial findings: refill epoch at 00:00 sees a large instantaneous accounting from the background sweep and keepalive pings. This consumes burst credits and leaves interactive routes without burst capacity for ~60–120s while refill smoothing catches up. Recommending immediate mitigations and a long-term isolation plan (see investigation_notes and resolution_notes).

2026-03-03 - SRE (Priya Nair): Investigation confirms that keepalive pings and readiness probes from k8s health checks were counted against tenant quota. Also observed minor clock skew (~2s) between some edge proxies causing small refill window drift; combined with fanout the effect is amplified. Proposal: 1) exempt internal health-check endpoints from rate accounting via route-level policy, 2) schedule sweep outside of refill boundary or use staggered startup, 3) configure dedicated burst pool for interactive routes or separate API key scope for background workers.

2026-03-04 - Maya Chen (Customer): We applied a quick workaround: staggered the sweep start by 10s per worker group and disabled the keepalive during the sweep. Early telemetry shows a drop in 429s. We'll implement separate API keys if recommended.

2026-03-05 - Support (Diego Alvarez): Marking resolved after customer confirmed success. Follow-up: submitted INT ticket to infra to add a runbook for dedicated pools about 'refill alignment and background-job isolation' and a console UX suggestion to show per-route burst pool usage.
investigation_notes: Pulled token-refill logs for tenant_id: ds-778; saw epoch spikes at 00:00 PDT on 2026-03-01 and 00:00 PDT on 2026-03-02 correlating with customer request IDs.
Observed a burst of ~150 concurrent short requests (50–200ms) plus ~150 keepalive pings within the first 30s of the refill epoch.
Rate-limiter accounting currently counts readiness/healthcheck endpoints; these were being called by orchestrator during the sweep and incrementing tenant token usage.
Edge proxy traces show ~2s clock skew between two ingress clusters which caused some refill-window misalignment; when combined with fanout this produced near-simultaneous accounting across shards.
No anomalies found in autoscaler logs for the dedicated pool; GPU availability and serving-runtime latency were normal during events.
Temporary mitigation (customer applied): staggered worker startups + disabling keepalive reduced immediate burst; observed falloff from ~6% 429 to <0.5% in subsequent runs.

Long-term configuration options evaluated: route-level burst isolation, separate API key scope for background workers, scheduling sweeps outside refill epoch, platform-side smoothing of refill epochs for dedicated pools, and explicit exemption rules for health-check endpoints.
Filed INT follow-up to consider default docs/console guidance for dedicated customers mixing background jobs and interactive lanes.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied and validated by customer: staggered sweep startup + disable keepalive during sweep reduced 429s to <0.5%. Recommended short-term actions for customer: 1) create a separate API key scoped to background workers to isolate accounting, 2) schedule sweep to start off-boundary from tenant refill epoch, or stagger worker start times by group. Recommended platform-side / long-term actions (internal): 1) provide an option to exempt health-check/keepalive endpoints from tenant token accounting via route policy, 2) add a console warning when a tenant's refill epoch coincides with a scheduled high-fanout job, 3) consider smoothing refill boundaries across shards for dedicated pools to reduce epoch-amplification on fanouts.

Follow-ups: INT-330 created to track runbook/doc updates and PR#2210 opened to prototype a route-exempt flag for health-check paths. Customer confirmed resolution on 2026-03-05 and is scheduling separate API keys as a durable fix.
next_steps: INT: Update dedicated-pool runbook with guidelines for mixing background workers and interactive lanes (assigned INT-330).
Engineering: Evaluate and prototype route-level exemption flag for health-check endpoints (PR#2210 reference).
Support/CS: Draft short KB article for customers on 'Avoiding refill-boundary spikes' with recommended config snippets and sample curl/route examples.
Customer: Implement separate API key for background workers and schedule future sweeps off-refill-window; Support to verify after change.
